sources.entry: ntfy - Push notifications to phone or desktop using HTTP PUT/POST, with Android app, CLI and web app, similar to Pushover and Gotify. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) Apache-2.0/GPL-2.0 Go/Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: The Android client app for ntfy, a service for receiving HTTP PUT/POST-based push notifications on a phone.
summary.what_it_does: This repository holds the Android app for ntfy (ntfy.sh), which the README says can be installed from F-Droid, the Play Store, or APK files on the GitHub releases page. The README states the APKs are signed with a specific SHA-256 certificate fingerprint and that the same fingerprint can be checked via DNS TXT records for ntfy.sh. It notes translations are managed through Weblate. Build instructions are not included in the README; it points to the official docs instead. The README also credits several third-party projects used as references or data sources, including an emoji.json file derived from github/gemoji.
use_cases: receive push notifications on an Android phone
get notifications from HTTP PUT/POST requests
translate an Android app via Weblate
how_to_run: Install the app from F-Droid or the Google Play Store
Or download the signed .apk from the GitHub releases page
notable: APKs signed with a published SHA-256 certificate fingerprint that can also be checked via DNS TXT records for ntfy.sh
Available on F-Droid, Google Play, and GitHub releases
Emoji support via an emoji.json file derived from gemoji
caveats: Build steps are not in the README; it refers to the official docs
Only the Android client is covered here; the server and CLI are separate projects
